# When Does a Designer Become a House? — motion and channel evidence manifest

Version 2.0 · RN Collins · 7 September 2026

## Reels / TikTok / Shorts
### 0–8s — OBJ-81112
Voiceover: The house is visible as both maker attribution and an enduring cataloguing unit.

Treatment: slow evidence push; no synthetic parallax

Credit: Gift of Mrs. Philip K. Rhinelander, 1946

Rights: Public Domain / Met Open Access

### 8–16s — B01-DIAGRAM-1
Voiceover: 01 · CODE — Can the eye be explained?. A code is not a mood board. It is a set of recurring decisions—silhouette, proportion, material, finish, behavior, refusal—with examples, exceptions, and a reason for each. The test is not whether every object looks alike. It is whether a collaborator can recognize the governing judgment.

Treatment: vertical reveal with source footer

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 16–24s — B01-DIAGRAM-2
Voiceover: 02 · CARRY — Can another hand act without impersonating?. An institution needs roles, handoffs, review rituals, and vocabulary. Documentation should transmit the standard while leaving room for skilled interpretation. If every decision must return to the founder, the practice has staff but not institutional capacity.

Treatment: slow evidence push; no synthetic parallax

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 24–32s — B01-DIAGRAM-3
Voiceover: 03 · PROOF — Can the work prove its own making?. Collection records, samples, specifications, correspondence, credits, rights decisions, and accession-quality metadata turn memory into evidence. The record does not replace the object; it prevents the object from becoming anonymous.

Treatment: vertical reveal with source footer

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

### 32–40s — B01-DIAGRAM-4
Voiceover: 04 · CONTINUITY — Can the system survive absence?. A house is tested by illness, departure, conflict, growth, sale, and succession. Continuity requires named authority, access to accounts and files, an archive, and a method for distinguishing evolution from imitation.

Treatment: slow evidence push; no synthetic parallax

Credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins

Rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
